land.text: Ifriqiya, whose governor Handhala ibn Safwan agreed in February 745 to return to Damascus rather than fight Ibn Habib

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Fihrid row starts only in 750, when its Umayyad shape ends; 745-749 is a new keyframe and probably overlaps the Umayyad shape.

land.text: Ifriqiya and Tripolitania, taken by the Warfajuma and Sufri Berbers (Kairouan, 757) and the Ibadites (Tripoli, 757)

successors.note: Cliopatria's Kharijites shape begins 757 and covers the whole Fihrid territory.

capitals.name: Kairouan (al-Qayrawan)
capitals.note: Infobox seat 'Al-Qayrawan (Ifriqiya)'; Ibn Habib 'installed himself in Kairouan' in 745 after proclaiming himself emir at Tunis in late 744 (Abd al-Rahman ibn Habib page). The infobox also lists Qurtubah (Cordoba) for the Fihrids of al-Andalus, which is not Cliopatria's Fihrid territory.

rulers.name: Abd al-Rahman ibn Habib al-Fihri
rulers.title: Emir of Ifriqiya
rulers.note: Murdered in 755 by his brother Ilyas ('plunging a dagger into his back').

rulers.name: Ilyas ibn Habib al-Fihri
rulers.title: Emir of Ifriqiya
rulers.note: The Fihrids page dates his emirate 755-756 in the genealogy; the Abd al-Rahman page has Habib deposing and killing him in late 755.

rulers.name: Habib ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Fihri
rulers.title: Emir of Ifriqiya
rulers.note: Final ruler; killed when the Warfajuma and Sufri Berbers took Kairouan in 757.

correction.text: Ifriqiya (Tunis, Kairouan) and Tripolitania seized by Ibn Habib in 744-745, without eastern Algeria

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Fihrids page gives 'Founded 745' but Cliopatria starts in 750 (when its Umayyad shape ends). Until 750 the caliph was Marwan II and the Umayyad shape probably still covers this land. The page: 'the western Maghreb - Morocco and eastern Algeria - remained out of his reach.'

correction.text: Ifriqiya and Tripolitania, without eastern Algeria

keyframe_review.note: 251,323 km2 (221,800 km2 at grid resolution), of which about 64,000 km2 lies in eastern Algeria (5.3-8.5 E): the page says 'the western Maghreb - Morocco and eastern Algeria - remained out of his reach', so Algeria is cut. 750 is also the year 'Ibn Habib then decided to revolt against the Abbasids' and 'dropped the name of the Abbasid caliph from the Friday prayers'. The page has no area to compare.

correction.text: Ifriqiya (Tunisia) in 751, with Tripolitania in the hands of the Ibadites; eastern Algeria cut

keyframe_review.note: 145,608 km2, Tunisia plus eastern Algeria without Libya. Two corrections: Algeria out, and valid for 751 only, because the page says 'in 752, Ibn Habib dispatched an Ifriqiyan army and reconquered Tripolitana from the Ibadites' (see the new 752 keyframe). The page does not date the Ibadite takeover (imam al-Harith 'revolted' after 747), so 751 is Cliopatria's.

correction.text: Ifriqiya and the reconquered Tripolitania, without eastern Algeria

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Tripolitania back under the Fihrids from 752; Cliopatria keeps it with the Kharijites until 754.

correction.text: Ifriqiya and Tripolitania under Ilyas and Habib ibn Abd al-Rahman, valid to 757

keyframe_review.note: 251,323 km2 again with the Algerian part (about 64,000 km2) cut. Years: the Fihrids page gives 'Dissolution: 757' and the Kharijite uprising of 757-758 that 'overrun and extinguished' the line, one year after Cliopatria's 756. 755 itself is the 'bloody family quarrel' that 'threw Ifriqiya into chaos'.

ledger.note: 745: Abd al-Rahman ibn Habib takes Ifriqiya. In late 744 he 'assembled a small force in Tunis and declared himself emir of Ifriqiya'; in February 745 the governor Handhala ibn Safwan 'agreed to return to Damascus rather than fight'; infobox 'Founded 745'.

region.text: Tripolitania, held by the Ibadites under their imam al-Harith

ledger.note: The page says only that the Ibadites revolted under al-Harith after Ilyas moved against them in 747, and that Tripolitania was reconquered in 752. 751 is Cliopatria's year for the Kharijite shape, not the page's.

region.text: Tripolitania, with the Ibadite remnants driven into the Jebel Nafusa

ledger.note: 752: Ibn Habib reconquers Tripolitania. 'In 752, Ibn Habib dispatched an Ifriqiyan army and reconquered Tripolitana from the Ibadites'; the remnants fled into the Jebel Nafusa.

757: Kairouan falls and the dynasty ends. 'Warfajuma Berbers and Sufrite allies captured Kairouan, killing Habib and ending the Fihrid dynasty'; the Fihrids page: the line was 'overrun and extinguished' in a Kharijite Berber uprising of 757-758.
757: the Ibadites under Abu al-Khattab al-Ma'afiri 'recaptured Tripoli'. The page names the city; the region is my reading.

region.text: the Fihrid emirate of Ifriqiya at its fall

ledger.note: 757: the Fihrid emirate of Ifriqiya ends. Infobox 'Dissolution: 757'; Habib ibn Abd al-Rahman, the final ruler, is killed at Kairouan. The Fihrids of al-Andalus lost Cordoba in 756 and are outside this dossier.

wars.name: Ibadite revolt in Tripolitania

zones.text: Tripolitania, with the Jebel Nafusa as refuge

wars.outcome: Ilyas ibn Habib moves against the Ibadites in 747; they rise under the imam al-Harith; in 752 an Ifriqiyan army reconquers Tripolitania and drives the remnants into the Jebel Nafusa.
wars.note: The page does not date the revolt itself; Cliopatria's 751-754 Kharijite shape sits in the same years.

wars.name: Kharijite conquest of Ifriqiya
wars.outcome: The Warfajuma and Sufri Berbers take Kairouan and kill Habib (757); the Ibadites under Abu al-Khattab al-Ma'afiri retake Tripoli (757) and Kairouan (758), founding the imamate.
wars.note: The Fihrids page: 'overrun and extinguished' in a Kharijite Berber uprising of 757-758. The Kharijites page dates the Ibadite seizure of Tripoli to 757 and of Kairouan to 758.

certainty.note: No frontier is named on the pages opened; the Maghrib frontier (eastern Algeria out of reach) and the Saharan edge are approximate.

sources.title: Fihrids
sources.note: Identity, dates 745/757, the genealogy of the emirs, the seat Kairouan, the end in the 757-758 Kharijite uprising.

sources.title: Abd al-Rahman ibn Habib al-Fihri
sources.note: The dated narrative 744-758: Tunis, Kairouan, the Abbasid break (750), the Ibadites and Tripolitania (747, 752), Ilyas 755, Kairouan 757, Tripoli 757, Kairouan 758, the western Maghreb out of reach.

sources.title: Kharijites
sources.note: Ibadi seizure of Tripoli 757 and Kairouan 758, the Abbasid expulsion in 761, Tahart.

notes: Cliopatria's Fihrid shape includes about 64,000 km2 of eastern Algeria (5.3-8.5 E); the Abd al-Rahman page says Morocco and eastern Algeria 'remained out of his reach' (undated, after the 740 Berber Revolt), so all four shapes are corrected by cutting Algeria. Tripolitania's holder in 750-751 is not dated: Cliopatria gives it to the Kharijites for 751-754 although the page has the Ibadite revolt 'later' than 747 and the reconquest in 752. The Fihrid row ends 756, the page 757; Cliopatria's Fihrid shape starts 750 although the emirate was proclaimed in late 744/745 (the Umayyad row probably covers 745-749; the Umayyad dossier of me-07 should be checked for overlap). The Fihrids page lists the Fihrids of al-Andalus (Yusuf ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Fihri, emir 747-756, deposed by Abd al-Rahman I who 'established the Umayyad Emirate of Qurtubah in 756'): that is not Cliopatria's Fihrid row and belongs to the Iberian group. Page budget 2 used: the Fihrids and Abd al-Rahman ibn Habib pages (the Kharijites page, opened for the Kharijites dossier, is cited for nothing here except as listed).
